'''Umpass-stay''' was a [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] into a life of [[Slavery/Legends|enslavement]] to the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clan]]. He grew up on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Shawti]], where he maintained the mud baths of local [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] leaders. Umpass-stay became the favorite of the Hutt [[Shebba Kalshi Desilijic]], and he became a personal [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] for the Hutt. His talent of judging the intentions of the people who approached Shebba proved [[Death/Legends|deadly]] when the Klatooinian misjudged the Hutt's nephew, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. After Shebba was killed, Umpass-stay was then offered a place in Jabba's [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]] as a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] in the Hutt's [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

Umpass-stay, alongside the drum master [[Ak-rev/Legends|Ak-rev]], performed with the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] when they came to Jabba's palace. In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Klatooinian performed the song "[[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]]" with the band just before [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], disguised as the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boushh/Legends|Boushh]], arrived with her bounty, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. After Jabba was killed by the Princess at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], Umpass-stay and Ak-rev set out for the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] to look for work. When the [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] they were traveling in was waylaid by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], the Klatooinian had to walk his way to Mos Eisley. Umpass-stay eventually served the Hutt [[Jocoro Desilijic Tiure]] on the planet [[Du Hutta]]. 

==Biography==
===Hutt favorite===
[[File:Umpass-stay_btm.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Umpass-stay played the drum alongside Ak-rev.]]
Umpass-stay, a [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] into a [[Umpass-stay's family|family]] enslaved to the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]], a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clan]],<ref name="DB" /> for centuries. On<ref name="SWTSE" /> the [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]<ref name="AOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Shawti system/Legends|Shawti system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Shawti]], he spent his [[Youngling/Legends|childhood]] on a large agricultural plantation. As he aged, he was trained in maintaining the mud baths of Hutt leaders local to the area. Umpass-stay soon became the favorite of the Hutt plantation leader [[Shebba Kalshi Desilijic]], gaining employ as first a [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] taster<ref name="SWTSE" /> and unofficial advisor<ref name="FF75">{{FactFile|75|MAX 7-10|Max Rebo Band}}</ref> and then a personal [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]]. As he silently watched Shebba, Umpass-stay learned the in-and-outs of Hutt business and discovered his talent for judging the intentions of those who came to the Hutt.<ref name="SWTSE" />

Shebba began to rely on the instincts of Umpass-stay, keeping him close by when dealing with relatives and associates. His instincts failed him<ref name="SWTSE" /> for the first time<ref name="FF75" /> when he misjudged Shebba's nephew, the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Jabba [[Death/Legends|assassinated]] Shebba, ending the bright future Umpass-stay once had. Though the Hutt had led the young Klatooinian to think his life would be over<ref name="SWTSE" /> at his hands,<ref name="FF75" /> Jabba offered him a new place in his [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|criminal empire]], even after hearing his name both praised and cursed in family circles. Umpass-stay traveled to<ref name="SWTSE" /> the Outer Rim planet<ref name="Complete Locations" /> [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he [[Spy/Legends|spied]] on members of Jabba's court<ref name="SWTSE" /> at the Hutt's [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]],<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Umpass-stay}}</ref> trying to find those who wanted to hurt the Hutt. In his spy duties, he served snacks to the court,<ref name="SWTSE" /> appearing like a typical goon or servant,<ref name="DB" /> and [[Musician/Legends|played]] a large<ref name="SWTSE" /> [[power drum]]<ref name="Complete Locations" /> alongside the [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] drum master [[Ak-rev/Legends|Ak-rev]]. The Weequay watched over his subordinate and spent many [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] playing<ref name="SWTSE" /> the card game<ref name="Sabacc">{{CSWECite|III|121|Sabacc}}</ref> [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] with him when Jabba slept in the [[Local day/Legends|afternoons]].<ref name="SWTSE" />

===Spying musician===
At one point,<ref name="SWTSE" /> Umpass-stay caught<ref name="Insider67">{{InsiderCite|67|Who's Who in the Max Rebo Band}}</ref> a team of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] hiding as a band of minstrels who aimed to kill Jabba. After that incident, Jabba insisted that all bands playing in the court incorporate Umpass-stay and his [[Drum/Legends|drum]]<ref name="SWTSE" /> for added protection.<ref name="DB" /> Most observers read this as just one of Jabba's eccentric decrees,<ref name="SWTSE" /> and not even<ref name="Insider67" /> Jabba's [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]]<ref name="SWTSE" /> [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] knew of Umpass-stay's purpose.<ref name="Insider67" /> Some bands didn't work in the drum on the principal of art, but Jabba didn't see this as a problem and forced them to perform within the palace's [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] pit. When word of Jabba's practice spread, the drum had a renaissance in the bands that worked in the palace and<ref name="SWTSE" /> the [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|Desilijic Complex]]<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="SWTSE" /> 

[[File:Rappertunie-WithBand-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|400px|Umpass-stay (between [[Rappertunie/Legends|Rappertunie]] and [[Lyn Me/Legends|Lyn Me]]) performed with the Max Rebo Band.]]
When the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] came to perform at Jabba's palace, the band was warned by Fortuna about Jabba's drum desires, but [[Ortolan/Legends|Ortolan]] Band leader [[Max Rebo/Legends|Max Rebo]] came prepared with several musical numbers incorporating the power drum.<ref name="SWTSE" /> Umpass-stay, Ak-rev, and the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] court member [[Doda Bodonawieedo/Legends|Doda Bodonawieedo]] were all ordered to sit in with the band by Jabba.<ref name="Insider67" /> Though a member of the band,<ref name="Insider67" /> the Klatooinian was only occasionally performed the drums with them.<ref name="FF75" />   

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]</ref> Umpass-stay and Ak-rev, with the rest of the Max Rebo Band, performed in the throne room of Jabba's palace. As their performance came to a close,<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> Jabba ordered his enslaved dancer, [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], to perform her dance again, but band singer [[Joh Yowza/Legends|Joh Yowza]] thought that Jabba was ordering the band to perform again, and the band kicked in<ref name="JN">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref> playing the song "[[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]]." During the performance, Jabba dropped Oola into the rancor pit<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> after she refused to sit with him,<ref name="JN" /> causing the band to stop. Shortly after the dancer was fed to his [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]], [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], disguised as the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boushh/Legends|Boushh]], entered the room with the Wookiee Chewbacca, her bounty. Organa and Chewbacca were both [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] members who had come to the palace to free the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], who was kept frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] in the throne room.<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> Umpass-stay and Ak-rev watched<ref name="Complete Locations" /> as Organa and Jabba negotiated over the price of the Wookiee.  Following a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] scare from the princess, a settlement was reached, causing the band to play<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> as the throne room party started up again.<ref name="JN" /> 

===Freed from Jabba===
That [[Local day/Legends|night]],<ref name="JN" /> Organa and Solo were captured by Jabba after the former was caught unfreezing the latter. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] came to the palace<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> the next morning<ref name="JN" /> asking for the release of his friends, though he failed and killed Jabba's rancor. Because of this, Skywalker, Solo, and Chewbacca were sentenced to death at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]].<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> As he was considered to be a lowly servant, Umpass-stay was not invited to travel among Jabba's entourage to the pit and thus did not get a chance to worn the Hutt about<ref name="SWTSE" /> "Tameel Skreej,"<ref name="Insider60">{{InsiderCite|60|Who's Who in Jabba's Palace}}</ref> a guard who was being watched very closely by the Klatooinian. "Skreej" was actually [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], a Rebel Alliance member who was posing<ref name="SWTSE" /> as a guard. At Carkoon, Jabba was killed by Organa,<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> freeing Umpass-stay from the Hutt's service.<ref name="DB" />  

When it was clear Jabba would not be returning, Umpass-stay and Ak-rev set out in a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] to Mos Eisley in an effort to find work. A band of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]],<ref name="Insider67" /> a [[Species/Legends|species]] indigenous to Tatooine,<ref name="SWTSE" /> ambushed<ref name="Insider67" /> and waylaid<ref name="SWTSE" /> the pair's speeder. The habit of Jabba's Weequay employees slaughtering [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]] to their god did not sit right with the indigenous people, as they worshiped banthas. The band let Umpass-stay go but beat Ak-rev to death and let his corpse to rot. Now without a speeder, food, or [[Water/Legends|water]], the Klatooinian had to walk nearly seventy [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] to Mos Eisley.<ref name="Insider67" />

[[File:Mos Eisley.png|thumb|right|400px|Umpass-stay walked nearly seventy kilometers to the city Mos Eisley (pictured) after Jabba's death.]]
At the city, he met the [[Frell spacer]] [[Darson Kinderlot]], who gave him passage to Hutt Space in exchange for work.<ref name="Insider67" /> The directionless<ref name="DB" /> Umpass-stay eventually ended up faithfully serving the Hutt [[Jocoro Desilijic Tiure]] on the planet [[Du Hutta]].<ref name="Insider67" /> Like many other young Klatooinians, Umpass-stay spent most of his life working in service to the Hutts<ref name="DB" /> and it seemed as if he was destined to remain a bodyguard for Hutts the remainder of it.<ref name="ActionFigure">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Action Figure Collection]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Umpass-stay was an energetic Klatooinian<ref name="DB" /> who was huge in size<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|279|Umpass-stay}}</ref> with [[Color/Legends|brown]] skin<ref name="DB" /> and black-colored [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="30thfigure" /> He had little interest in music<ref name="Insider67" /> and believed the Hutts were gods because of their long lifespan.<ref name="30thfigure" /> The Klatooinian was a trusted individual to both Shebba and Jabba.<ref name="CSWE" />

==Skills and abilities==
Umpass-stay was trained in maintaining the mud baths of Hutt leaders local to Shawti. When he worked as a bodyguard to Shebba, he was trained in many self-defense techniques to better serve the Hutt. Umpass-stay also had a talent for judging the intentions of those who approached Shebba, though he misjudged Jabba, leading to the Shebba's death.<ref name="SWTSE" /> While he worked with Jabba, Umpass-stay was an average musician who was a better spy.<ref name="Insider67" />

The Klatooinian had fighting skills, including melee combat and parrying, brawling, and [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] usage. Other non-combat skills of his included playing the drum, dodging, searching, and sneaking. Not redistricted to just physical ability, Umpass-stay had some skill in conning beings and was educated on survival, streetwise knowledge, and other [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="SWTSE" />

==Equipment==
Umpass-stay utilized a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. When playing<ref name="SWTSE" /> the power drum<ref name="Complete Locations" /> with Ak-rev, he used a drum mallet.<ref name="SWTSE" /> While performing with the Max Rebo Band<ref name="SpecialEdition" /> in 4 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Klatooinian wore a black [[Clothing/Legends|shirt]] with white sleeves and tan padding, gray pants, and brown shoes. In addition, he also wore black chest [[Armor/Legends|armor]] with red sashes, a tan [[Belt/Legends|belt]] with pouches, spiked brown bracers, and a tan head wrapping.<ref name="30thfigure" />  

==Behind the scenes==
===A drummer joins the band===
{{Quote|I was able to add back-up singers, more horn players, some drummers, and those kinds of things to make it much more lively and bigger musical number.|George Lucas, on some of his additions to ''Return of the Jedi''|<ref name="MakingMagic" />}}
Umpass-stay was created for<ref name="MakingMagic" /> the ''[[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]]'' re-release of the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return to the Jedi'']],<ref name="SpecialEdition">{{Film|VI}}</ref> which released on [[March 14]], [[1997]].<ref name="A Gift For Boba Fett">{{ThisWeek|KUPQ8aT8bJU|Marvel Comics Previews, Unwrapping a Gift for Boba Fett, and More!}}</ref> Added to film under the direction of ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]], several pieces of concept art were created for the character.<ref name="MakingMagic" /> In one artwork, Umpass-stay was drawn as a four-[[Limb/Legends|armed]] alien playing the drum with their club-like hands.<ref name="DB" /> [[Lucasfilm]] art director [[Doug Chiang]] prepared a preliminary composite using the artwork that showed what the "Jabba Rocks" sequence would look like with all digital character additions. As the digital characters were costly and time-taking, a mixture of puppets, actors, and computer animation was decided for the Max Rebo Band.<ref name="Chiang">{{Topps|set=1997 Topps Star Wars Special Edition Widevision|cardname=
#71 - Int. Tatooine - Jabba's Palace - Behind-the-Scenes
|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73004/cid/5259735/1997-Topps-Widevision-The-Star-Wars-Trilogy-Special-Edition-71-Int.-Tatooine---Jabba's-Palace---Behind-the-Scenes|archivedate=20260817220904}}</ref>

Two other artworks showed a Weequay drummer with drum mallets and a body type similar to Umpass-stay's. The Weequay character was changed into a Klatooinian with another piece that included a note for usage of a "BARADA MASK." Artist [[Derek Thompson]] drew the next artwork, dated to [[May]] of [[1996]]. It identified the character as "Drummer 1," and showed him as a member of the [[Kajain'sa'Nikto/Legends|Kajain'sa'Nikto]] species with an outfit close to what Umpass-stay wore in the finished film. A colorized piece of the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] iteration of the character, also by Thompson, was produced on [[May 7]], 1996. One artwork, labeled "JEDI DRUMMERS," showed two identical alien drummers with dual drum mallets.<ref name="MakingMagic" /> 

Umpass-stay's wardrobe was newly crafted for the ''Special Edition'', but his face and hands were original ''Return of the Jedi'' props taken from the [[Lucasfilm Archives]]. Umpass-stay's and Ak-rev's drumming styles were attained from the Japanese practice of [[Wikipedia:Taiko|Taiko]],<ref name="DBAk-rev">{{DB|character|akrev|Ak-rev}}</ref><ref name="DB" /> and the scene featuring the character was filmed on a partial recreation of the original set of Jabba's throne room<ref name="SWArchives">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]''</ref> at an [[Industrial Light & Magic]] soundstage.<ref name="ILM">{{Topps|set=1997 Topps Star Wars Special Edition Widevision|cardname=#70 - Int. Tatooine - Jabba's Palace - Behind-the-Scenes|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73004/cid/5259734/1997-Topps-Widevision-The-Star-Wars-Trilogy-Special-Edition-70-Int.-Tatooine---Jabba's-Palace---Behind-the-Scenes}}</ref>

===Reveal, naming, and continuity===
Prior to the re-release, the character was first pictured in the [[1996]] interactive CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Making Magic]]'', published by [[LucasArts]].<ref name="MakingMagic">''[[Star Wars: Making Magic]]''</ref> The character was later first identified in ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'', a supplement for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''<ref name="SWTSE" /> published in [[October]] 1997.<ref name="SWGC1">{{CollectorCite|1|Playing A Major Role}}</ref>

[[File:Wironicc.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Umpass-stay's image was used to represent Gamall Wironicc.]]
An image of Umpass-stay was used to portray the character [[Gamall Wironicc]] in<ref name="TatooineLimited" /> the [[May 11]], [[2001]]<ref name="Decipher">{{Decipher|url=starwars/expansions/tatooine|text=Tatooine}}</ref> ''[[Tatooine Limited]]'' expansion set to the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] by [[Decipher]].<ref name="TatooineLimited">{{CCG|set=Tatooine Limited|cardname=Gamall Wironicc}}</ref> [[Holocron continuity database]] maintainer [[Leland Chee]] announced in [[2011]] that he planned to [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] Wironicc as one of the unidentified Klatooinians seen in the background of the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="KotC">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=permalink.php?story_fbid=232130050141262&id=793375187#!/permalink.php?story_fbid=231138123573788&id=1152097426|author=Leland Chee|date=2011-07-07|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In Umpass-stay's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry posted on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="DB" /> on [[December 18]], 2001,<ref name="GooNeeTay">{{SWArchive|url=databank/news/2001/12/news20011218.html|text=''Goo Nee Tay!''}}</ref> the text incorrectly states that the band of minstrels caught by the Klatooinian were sitting in with the Max Rebo Band,<ref name="DB" /> which cannot be the case as it is anachronistic to the events introduced in the ''Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook''.<ref name="SWTSE" />
